channel.title: The Grant Desk - Artist Residencies, Media Arts, Film & Sound, US, weekly digest
channel.description: Paid open calls, fellowships and residencies in AI, tech, research, and digital and mixed-media arts, sorted into the right pile. Updated as new calls land on the desk. Filtered to: Artist Residencies, Media Arts, Film & Sound, US, weekly digest. Released weekly: each Sunday's drop carries one entry per grant added in the week before it (Sunday to Saturday). A call that closes before its drop goes out is not sent; the website lists those.

item.title: Schomburg Center Scholars-in-Residence 2027-28 (NYPL, Harlem; USD 35,000 long-term or USD 3,000 a month short-term; playwrights and creative writers eligible) (closes 1 Dec)
item.description:
Schomburg Center for Research in Black Culture, The New York Public Library
Deadline: 1 Dec 2026, 23:59 EST
Award: Long-term fellowship: USD 35,000 stipend. Short-term fellowship: USD 3,000 per month for one to three months. No application fee mentioned.

Residential fellowships for work on the history, politics, literature and culture of peoples of African descent that needs the Schomburg Center's collections.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Charles Allis Art Museum Artist in Residence 2027, Milwaukee (USD 1,800 honorarium, housing, meals and a museum-wide exhibition) (closes 4 Dec)
item.description:
Charles Allis Art Museum
Deadline: 4 Dec 2026
Award: USD 1,800 artist honorarium plus up to USD 400 travel stipend; furnished studio apartment, meals and light tools and materials provided. No application fee mentioned.

One artist is invited to work with the Charles Allis Art Museum's collection of more than 800 early twentieth-century pieces and to make an exhibition that runs through the whole of the historic Allis home, a 1911 Tudor-style mansion in Milwaukee.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: WHATIF: five-month digital art residency at NODE Studio NYC (USD 25,000 stipend) (closes 10 Dec)
item.description:
NODE Foundation
Deadline: 10 Dec 2026
Award: USD 5,000 monthly stipend for five months (USD 25,000 total; a collective shares one stipend), a dedicated workspace, technical support, and flights and lodging for a visit to the Palo Alto headquarters. Housing, relocation, local transport, living expenses, health insurance and visa sponsorship are not included. No application fee mentioned.

WHATIF is a five-month residency at NODE Studio NYC for people who want to pursue one burning question through digital art and technology. NODE Foundation runs a digital art space in Palo Alto and a studio in New York. WHO: anyone aged 18 or over.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: W. E. B. Du Bois Research Institute Fellows Program 2027-28 (Hutchins Center, Harvard; USD 70,000 to 75,000 for the academic year) (closes 14 Dec)
item.description:
W. E. B. Du Bois Research Institute, Hutchins Center for African and African American Research, Harvard University
Deadline: 14 Dec 2026
Award: Stipends of USD 70,000 to USD 75,000 for the ten-month academic year, adjusted for one-semester fellowships. Health insurance is not provided. No application fee.

The Fellows Program is the oldest activity of the W. E. B. Du Bois Research Institute, which has appointed fellows since 1975.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Ox-Bow Summer Fellowship 2027: twelve-week live-work fellowship in Michigan (USD 300 weekly stipend, room, board and studio) (closes 3 Jan 2027)
item.description:
Ox-Bow School of Art and Artists' Residency
Deadline: 3 Jan 2027
Award: USD 300 weekly stipend for twelve weeks, a travel stipend for arrival and departure (amount not published), a private room, all meals and a dedicated studio. In exchange fellows work 20 hours a week on campus operations. No application fee is mentioned.

Ox-Bow's Summer Fellowship is a twelve-week live-work programme on its lagoon-side campus in Saugatuck, Michigan.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Drama League: Beatrice Terry Residency 2027 for women and nonbinary writer-directors (USD 4,000 plus collaborator stipends, Hubbard Hall, NY) (closes 4 Jan 2027)
item.description:
The Drama League, in partnership with Hubbard Hall Center for the Arts and Education
Deadline: 4 Jan 2027
Award: USD 4,000 to the recipient; up to four collaborators receive USD 950 each (USD 3,800 total); up to USD 1,000 travel reimbursement; an optional USD 1,000 towards an industry reading in New York City within two years; housing at Hubbard Hall. No application fee mentioned.

A one-week generative residency for a director who is also the writer or adapter of the piece, used to produce an early draft of a new work for live performance that they intend to direct. One residency is awarded each year.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: McKnight National Residency and Commission 2027-28 (Playwrights' Center; USD 15,000 commission plus up to USD 12,250 in workshop funds) (closes 14 Jan 2027)
item.description:
Playwrights' Center, funded by the McKnight Foundation
Deadline: 14 Jan 2027, 23:59 CST
Award: USD 15,000 commission, plus up to USD 12,250 in workshop funds to develop the play, including travel and housing. No application fee mentioned.

A commission for one nationally recognised playwright from outside Minnesota to write a new play, developed through workshops at the Playwrights' Center and ending in a public reading.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Sculpture Space 2028 Artist Residency: two months in Utica, New York (USD 1,000 stipend, housing and shared studio) (closes 15 Jan 2027)
item.description:
Sculpture Space
Deadline: 15 Jan 2027
Award: USD 1,000 stipend per resident artist (two-person collaborative teams share one stipend), nearby housing and studio access. Application fee USD 35.

Founded in 1976, Sculpture Space is an international residency in Utica, New York, for artists working in sculpture and related three-dimensional practices. WHO: artists from the United States and internationally; two-person collaborative teams can apply and share one stipend.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Roman J. Witt Residency 2027-28 (University of Michigan Stamps School and UMMA; USD 20,000 honorarium, housing, studio and a museum exhibition) (closes 25 Jan 2027)
item.description:
University of Michigan Stamps School of Art & Design and University of Michigan Museum of Art (UMMA)
Deadline: 25 Jan 2027
Award: USD 20,000 honorarium for up to twelve weeks in residence, plus housing, studio space and up to USD 5,000 for materials, research and development. Travel support is limited. SlideRoom charges a USD 15 processing fee for media uploads.

One residency a year for a visiting artist or designer to make new work at the Stamps School while engaging the university community, ending in an exhibition at UMMA's Irving Stenn, Jr. Family Gallery, a 1,200-square-foot, glass-walled, street-facing space beside a main campus route.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Fine Arts Work Center Visual Arts Fellowship 2027-28: seven months in Provincetown (USD 1,300 monthly stipend, apartment and studio) (closes 7 Feb 2027)
item.description:
Fine Arts Work Center in Provincetown
Deadline: 7 Feb 2027
Award: USD 1,300 monthly stipend for seven months, a USD 1,000 exit stipend to support relocation, a furnished apartment and a studio of about 400 square feet. Application fee USD 40 to 65 depending on date (USD 55 until 1 December, then USD 65); limited fee waivers on request.

The Fine Arts Work Center gives emerging visual artists seven months of time, housing and a studio in Provincetown, on the tip of Cape Cod. WHO: visual artists aged 18 or over at an early stage of their careers. No MFA is required.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Mabou Mines SUITE/space Residency 2027-2029 (NYC early-career interdisciplinary performance, two USD 4,000 stipends) (closes 22 Nov)
item.description:
Mabou Mines
Deadline: 22 Nov 2026, 23:59 EST
Award: Two USD 4,000 stipends (dependent on funding), plus 100 hours of rehearsal space and technical support. No application fee.

SUITE/space is Mabou Mines' two-year performance residency for early-career interdisciplinary artists in New York whose practices come from lived experiences at the margins. WHO: NYC-based early-career interdisciplinary performance artists.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: WVU Libraries Artist in Residence 2027: Common Threads, Industry, Labor and Community (USD 1,000 honorarium) (closes 30 Nov)
item.description:
West Virginia University Libraries
Deadline: 30 Nov 2026
Award: USD 1,000 honorarium plus up to USD 1,000 materials and up to USD 3,000 travel and lodging. No application fee.

An archive-based residency in which the artist works with WVU Libraries' union records and oral histories on industry, labor and community. Digital media is eligible. ELIGIBILITY: US- and Canada-based artists aged 18 and over.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Kent Cultural Alliance SFW Residency, Spring 2027 "SERVICE": six-week live-in residency in Chestertown, Maryland (USD 7,500 stipend) (closes 1 Dec)
item.description:
Kent Cultural Alliance
Deadline: 1 Dec 2026, 17:00 EST
Award: USD 7,500 stipend for the six-week session, travel reimbursed up to USD 1,000, studio and gallery expenses reimbursed up to USD 1,500, and on-site housing with a private en-suite bedroom. No application fee.

A community-engaged residency on Maryland's Eastern Shore. Three artists live and work for six weeks in the Raimond Cultural Center, a restored historic house, around the theme SERVICE, working with local partners For All Seasons, the Kent County Food Pantry and Sumner Hall.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Glen Foerd Artist in Residence 2027: year-long residency for a Philadelphia performance artist or collective (USD 3,000 stipend) (closes 6 Dec)
item.description:
Glen Foerd
Deadline: 6 Dec 2026, 23:59 EST
Award: USD 3,000 stipend for materials, time and costs, paid in three instalments. USD 10 application fee, waived on request.

Glen Foerd, a riverside historic estate in Philadelphia, selects one Philadelphia-based performance artist or collective for its 2027 residency. Performance is read broadly: music, theatre, film and social practice all count.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Petrides Residency for a Greek Artist in NY (NYFA x ISCP): funded three-month Brooklyn studio residency (USD 9,000 stipend) (closes 8 Dec)
item.description:
New York Foundation for the Arts (NYFA) with sculptor George Petrides and the International Studio & Curatorial Program (ISCP)
Deadline: 8 Dec 2026, 17:00 EST
Award: Fully funded three-month residency with a private studio, a USD 9,000 stipend, a USD 1,000 travel payment and up to USD 300 for professional development. Housing is not arranged by ISCP. No application fee stated.

NYFA, sculptor George Petrides and the International Studio & Curatorial Program (ISCP) offer one Greek artist a fully funded three-month studio residency in Brooklyn.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Craigardan Trillium Fellowship 2027 (residency for artists, activists and scholars of color, USD 4,600 + USD 500 honorarium) (closes 15 Dec)
item.description:
Craigardan
Deadline: 15 Dec 2026
Award: USD 4,600 fellowship toward a minimum two-week residency (covers the residency fee), plus a USD 500 honorarium. Travel, materials and personal expenses are not covered. USD 25 application fee (waivers available on request).

The Trillium Fellowship supports artists, activists and scholars of color working in any discipline who would benefit from the time and space to pursue their work or find creative retreat at Craigardan, a residency and farm in the Adirondacks.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: EFA SHIFT x Momus Residency 2027: six-month programme for New York artists who write and writers who make art (USD 2,000 honorarium) (closes 15 Dec)
item.description:
Elizabeth Foundation for the Arts (EFA Studios) with Momus
Deadline: 15 Dec 2026
Award: Artist honorarium of USD 2,000, within a six-month residency at EFA Studios with monthly critical seminars and mentoring. No application fee stated.

A new iteration of EFA's SHIFT Residency, run with the art criticism platform Momus and focused on where artistic practice meets critical writing.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: SPACES: Echo Artist Residency (Cleveland, paired residency with honorarium and production budget) (closes 10 Feb 2027)
item.description:
SPACES
Deadline: 10 Feb 2027
Award: Artist honorarium and production budget plus lodging in the gallery. SPACES does not publish figures; the Alliance of Artists Communities listing gives a USD 2,000 artist stipend plus USD 500 for travel and materials. No application fee.

Echo is a paired residency at SPACES in Cleveland: each season it selects one Northeast Ohio artist (Cuyahoga and contiguous counties) and one artist from outside the region as a peer cohort, preferring complementary or intersecting themes, though collaboration is not required.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Kala Art Institute: Media Arts Fellowship 2027-28 (Berkeley; USD 3,000 stipend) (closes 1 Mar 2027)
item.description:
Kala Art Institute
Deadline: 1 Mar 2027
Award: USD 3,000 stipend plus facility access.

Kala's long-running Media Arts Fellowship supports four artists working in film and video, sound, animation, performance cinema and media installation. ELIGIBILITY: local, national and international artists not enrolled in a degree programme.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Bernheim Arboretum and Research Forest: Artist in Residence 2027 (Kentucky, USD 2,500 stipend) (closes 30 Nov)
item.description:
Bernheim Arboretum and Research Forest (Arts in Nature programme)
Deadline: 30 Nov 2026
Award: USD 2,500 stipend, plus a furnished one-bedroom cabin (kitchen, bath, Wi-Fi), a studio near a 32-acre lake, staff support, and free or discounted classes and events. No application fee stated.

Annual residency in which artists live at Bernheim Arboretum and Research Forest and create site-specific work inspired by total immersion in the natural environment. WHO: visual and mixed-media artists, including those working with sound and with performance that incorporates visual elements.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Museum of Fine Arts, Houston: Core Residency Program 2027-29 (USD 100,000 over 23 months, artists and critical writers) (closes 8 Jan 2027)
item.description:
Core Residency Program, Glassell School of Art, Museum of Fine Arts, Houston (MFAH)
Deadline: 8 Jan 2027
Award: USD 100,000 (USD 50,000 per year) plus a health and wellness stipend, private studio, and free or discounted Glassell School classes. Application fee USD 12.

Two-year residency for exceptional, highly motivated emerging artists and critical writers committed to developing a sustainable practice.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: School for Advanced Research: Native Artist Fellowships 2027 (USD 15,000 plus Santa Fe residency) (closes 15 Jan 2027)
item.description:
School for Advanced Research, Indian Arts Research Center
Deadline: 15 Jan 2027
Award: USD 15,000 stipend plus housing, studio space, a supplies allowance and travel. No application fee stated.

The Indian Arts Research Center at the School for Advanced Research offers three residential fellowships for Native American artists: the Eric and Barbara Dobkin Fellowship for Native women artists working in any media (including digital art and film/video), the Ronald and Susan Dubin Fellowship...

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Adirondack Experience (ADKX) Artist-in-Residence 2027
item.description: Adirondack Experience, The Museum on Blue Mountain Lake (ADKX) · deadline 11 Dec 2026 · USD 5,000 stipend per one-month residency, plus USD 500 travel allowance, USD 250 Art Lab materials allowance, and free on-site housing with utilities, wi-fi and laundry included.
